quarterly_data.signal: Relay's Q2 2026 results release: revenue was $0.4 million versus $0.7 million in Q2 2025, recognized under its Exclusive License Agreement with Elevar Therapeutics. R&D expenses were $76.5 million versus $63.9 million; the increase of $12.6 million was primarily due to increases in costs across ongoing clinical trials for zovegalisib, partially offset by the impact from strategic choices made to streamline the research organization prior to 2026. Net loss was $83.7 million. Relay expects its cash, cash equivalents and investments of $910.9 million to fund operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue $0.4 million vs $0.7 million; R&D $76.5 million vs $63.9 million; net loss $83.7 million; cash runway into 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Pfizer (supplier): Relay selected zovegalisib plus atirmociclib as its go-forward triplet regimen for first-line breast cancer and announced a clinical supply agreement with Pfizer, under which Pfizer agreed to supply atirmociclib for the experimental arm and the palbociclib portion of the control arm of the planned study; Relay retains full global rights for zovegalisib. The Phase 3 first-line trial in endocrine-sensitive patients is expected to initiate in early 2027, subject to regulatory feedback. Relay also expects a regulatory update to confirm the design of that trial by year-end 2026 and a data update for the Phase 1/2 triplet combination in 1H 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Phase 3 first-line trial expected to initiate in early 2027; triplet data update 1H 2027
